turns.user: why are the romanian deadlifts after the squats and not before
turns.reply:
Squats come first because they're a Tier 1 compound lift requiring heavy axial loading and full-body coordination. Putting them first lets you attack the highest-skill, highest-fatigue movement with fresh legs and maximum central nervous system focus.

Romanian deadlifts target the posterior chain (glutes and hamstrings) with a hip hinge pattern. Doing them second means your quads are already fatigued from squatting, allowing you to load the hams and glutes effectively without your quads taking over the movement.

If you ever flipped the order, the hamstring fatigue from RDLs would compromise your pelvic stability and leg drive on the back squat, increasing injury risk when supporting the bar.
